open_points.subject: configuration and credential path traversal
open_points.text: the path is opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any of them, each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`
open_points.question: Which flags and directory-relative mechanism are used for intermediate components, and must an execute-only but unreadable directory component be accepted or refused?
options: Open intermediate directories with `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` and subsequent components relative to their descriptors
Open intermediate directories read-only with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`, refusing execute-only directories
Use another component-walking combination that preserves the no-symlink guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Use directory-relative opens with `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` for intermediate components.

open_points.subject: configuration and credential path components
open_points.text: the path is opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any of them
open_points.question: How are empty, `.` and `..` components in the absolute configuration or secret-file path handled: traversed literally, normalized, or refused?
options: Refuse any `.` or `..` component and ignore only the leading empty component of an absolute path
Traverse `.` and `..` component by component
Normalize the path before opening it
open_points.default_guess: Refuse `.` and `..` components and handle the leading root separately.

open_points.subject: store path traversal after start
open_points.text: Every file of the directory the store opens itself is opened without following symbolic links, with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW` on every open ... A link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written.
open_points.question: How does a store call detect and refuse a symlink inserted into an ancestor directory after start, given that `O_NOFOLLOW` on the final file open does not prevent following symlinked path components?
options: Open every component relative to held directory descriptors with `O_NOFOLLOW`
Hold trusted descriptors for all store directories from start and use only descriptor-relative opens
Limit the later-link guarantee to the final component
open_points.default_guess: Hold trusted directory descriptors and use descriptor-relative, no-follow opens for every component.

open_points.subject: SQLite database and journal symlinks
open_points.text: The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link ... A link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written.
open_points.question: If the database or journal path is replaced by a symlink after the start walk but before SQLite opens it, must the call refuse with nothing written, or are SQLite-managed files exceptions to the later-symlink rule and the formal invariant `symlink_inside(data_directory) -> refused`?
options: The later-symlink guarantee and formal invariant include SQLite files, requiring a mechanism that prevents the race
SQLite-managed files are explicit exceptions and may be followed if changed by the kernel user after the walk
The kernel stops or otherwise refuses all store use when it cannot re-establish that SQLite opened the checked files
open_points.default_guess: Treat the guarantee as applying to SQLite files too and require a race-free opening or containment mechanism.

open_points.subject: SQLite auxiliary files
open_points.text: The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite
open_points.question: Which SQLite-created files are covered by “its journal”—a rollback journal, WAL and shared-memory files, temporary databases, or every auxiliary file SQLite may create—and do all receive the stated exception?
options: Only a rollback-journal file is allowed
The database, rollback journal, WAL and shared-memory files are allowed
Every SQLite auxiliary or temporary file inside the data directory is covered
open_points.default_guess: Cover the database plus the configured journal mode's rollback-journal or WAL/shared-memory files, and disallow other SQLite temporary files in the data directory.

open_points.subject: Linux-only host restriction
open_points.text: The kernel does not test the host: on any other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start stops
open_points.question: What enforces the Linux-only rule if a non-Linux host or compatibility environment can make the sandbox probe succeed, and what definition of “host” determines whether that environment is allowed?
options: Probe success defines an acceptable Linux execution environment regardless of the underlying host
The kernel must verify that the running operating system is Linux in addition to the probe
Release packaging, rather than the kernel, enforces the host restriction
open_points.default_guess: Treat the operating environment visible to the kernel as the host and explicitly require it to identify as Linux before running the probe.

open_points.subject: pinned sandbox runtime on accepted Linux hosts
open_points.text: A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of the sandbox runtime ... any Linux on which that probe passes is a host
open_points.question: May a Linux host whose installed sandbox runtime has a different version run the release when its probe passes, or must the exact pinned runtime version also be established?
options: Probe success is sufficient even when the installed runtime version differs
The kernel verifies the exact pinned runtime version before the probe
The release supplies its own pinned runtime, so the host-installed version is never selected
open_points.default_guess: The release supplies or selects the exact pinned runtime and refuses to use a different installed version.
